title: Yamada-kun and the Seven Witches
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Bored delinquent Ryu Yamada falls down a staircase onto honor student Urara Shiraishi and discovers that a kiss makes them swap bodies. Through the revived Supernatural Studies club he finds seven school 'witches' whose powers are all triggered by kissing, and is pulled into student-council politics, memory erasure and a growing romance with Urara.
life_message: It holds up friendship and loyalty as what turns isolated outcasts into people who belong.

content.note: Delinquent scuffles and a near-fire at the old schoolhouse (Wikipedia; AniList Delinquents).
Memory-erasure plots and school schemes; light mystery tone (Wikipedia).
Kissing drives every power; one-way fan service in body-swap scenes (Fandom Post; Ecchi genre; MangaDex suggestive). Kodansha rates it 16+.
Urara is isolated and bullied before the swap (MangaUpdates Bullying; Fandom Post on social outcasts).
Kissing classmates, often without warning, to trigger powers; using the swap to cheat on tests (Fandom Post).

dominant: Communitarianism (club as found family), Pragmatism, Expressive individualism

delivery.note: Its view of friendship and belonging is carried by the club's adventures within a body-swap comedy.

winners_losers: Loyal outcasts win friendship and love, while manipulative student-council and Shogi-club schemers lose. The story's sympathy goes to belonging and loyalty over rules and status.
